findings.finding: The heldout-file migration inventory in AC #3 enumerates `test_unrelated_same_named_attribute_keeps_the_gate_quiet`, `test_every_real_receiver_shape_counts_as_a_read`, and the shared `_SCHEMA` fixture as edit targets, but omits `test_main_exit_codes_and_output` (tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_heldout.py:135), which also consumes `_SCHEMA` and asserts `rc2 == 0` on the clean-path reader `c.s.ghost_knob` (line 147). That reader spells the section attribute `s`; the other migrated tests use `.section.`. Once `_SCHEMA` gains a root `Config` whose section field is named to match `.section.`, the `.s.` receiver resolves to no owner under the new owner-resolution contract, so `ghost_knob` reads as unread, `main` returns 1, and the `assert rc2 == 0` at line 151 fails.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC #3 ('BOTH existing gate test files are MIGRATED ...'), heldout-file bullet
findings.suggested_fix: Name test_main_exit_codes_and_output as a third heldout edit target and either rename the `_SCHEMA` section field to `s` (matching every receiver used across the heldout tests) or update this test's reader to `c.section.ghost_knob` so its receiver resolves to the section-owning class.

findings.finding: AC #3's test-migration inventory enumerates which tests/schema constants to migrate to the owner-resolution contract but omits test_main_exit_codes_and_output (tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_heldout.py:135-152), whose clean-path reader `c.s.ghost_knob` (line 147) will break under owner resolution. Its receiver `.s` differs from the `.section` spelling used by the receiver-shape tests (lines 57-60) that the AC provisions the _SCHEMA root Config section field for, so `c.s` will not bind to SectionConfig, ghost_knob will be reported unread, and the clean assertion `rc2 == 0` (line 151) will fail.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, 3rd checklist item ('The existing gate tests are MIGRATED to the owner-resolution contract ... the synthetic schemas `_SCHEMA_ONE_FIELD` / `_SCHEMA` gain a root `Config` dataclass + section field ... and each receiver shape in `test_every_real_receiver_shape_counts_as_a_read` is kept passing ...')
findings.suggested_fix: In AC #3, name test_main_exit_codes_and_output alongside test_every_real_receiver_shape_counts_as_a_read and specify that its clean-path reader's receiver be made resolvable (e.g. change `c.s.ghost_knob` to use the same section attribute name given to _SCHEMA's root Config, or annotate `c` / the section local to SectionConfig).

findings.finding: The 'Design of the fix' introduces a bespoke AST resolver culminating in a cross-module fixed point that binds unannotated parameters from their call sites -- effectively a purpose-scoped points-to/type-inference analysis -- without considering established prior art for receiver->owning-class resolution, even though mypy is already installed and invoked by this plan's own `make typecheck` AC.
findings.location: Design of the fix (steps 2–3) and 'Failure direction, stated honestly'
scenarios: A reviewer asks why the gate re-implements parameter-to-type binding rather than querying mypy, which the repo already runs.
The hand-rolled fixed point misses a receiver shape that mypy would resolve, newly (falsely) flagging a live field and breaking CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert a short paragraph noting that mypy (already a dev dependency, run by `make typecheck`) and jedi/pyright can resolve a receiver expression to its declaring class, and explain the trade-off chosen: a self-contained, dataclass-scoped AST resolver is preferred for a fast, hermetic CI gate over invoking a full type-check pass — while acknowledging the cross-module fixed point re-implements a slice of what those tools already do.
